findings.english_quote: all loudly proclaiming every kind of guilty conscience.
findings.issue: The note discusses moral conscience and unscrupulousness but omits the material alternative sense of δυσσυνειδησία as difficulty of comprehension or unintelligibility. That alternative is especially relevant after the sequence describing the statements as senseless, ambiguous, crooked, and unclear. The moral interpretation can be understood as the statements exposing their speaker's fraudulent conscience, but the note does not explain that contextual choice against the comprehension reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note preserving the alternative, for example: “Alternatively, ‘all loudly proclaiming utter unintelligibility,’ taking δυσσυνειδησία as difficulty of comprehension and continuing the preceding descriptions of obscurity. The main moral reading instead takes the distorted and appropriated statements as exposing their speaker's conscience.” Explicitly compare these candidates before retaining or replacing the main wording. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: And all the same, they hate and flee
findings.issue: In this English construction, “all the same” is concessive, meaning “nevertheless.” The supplied ὁμῶς ordinarily expresses likeness or equality, whereas the familiar concessive adverb is ὅμως. The note lists “alike” and “all the same” without distinguishing the English phrase's concessive force or explaining a supported concessive interpretation of the supplied spelling. Its appeal to irony does not by itself establish that lexical shift. This is an interpretive issue with verified print, not evidence of an OCR defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer the source-transparent candidate “And they likewise hate and flee those who have greater compassion for them and pursue them in order to benefit them.” If retaining “all the same,” document the basis for interpreting the printed ὁμῶς concessively and explicitly distinguish that interpretation from any proposed correction to ὅμως. Do not silently change the Greek; the proposed English must undergo fresh review.
